items.competency: Code of Conduct and Ethical Standards (R.A. 6713)
items.stem: Under R.A. 6713, when must a covered public employee file the Statement of Assets, Liabilities and Net Worth (SALN)?

options.text: Within 30 days after assuming office, on or before April 30 every year, and within 30 days after leaving the service
Within 60 days after assuming office, on or before April 15 every year, and within 60 days after leaving the service
Within 30 days after assuming office, on or before December 31 every year, and within one year after leaving the service
Within 15 working days after assuming office, on or before June 30 every year, and only if asked after leaving the service

reveal.terms: SALN: sworn statement of assets, liabilities, net worth and business interests (Sec. 8).
reveal.why_correct: Answer: Within 30 days after assuming office, on or before April 30 every year, and within 30 days after leaving the service. Sec. 8(A) sets three filing points: (a) within 30 days after assumption of office, (b) on or before April 30 of every year thereafter, and (c) within 30 days after separation from the service.

why_wrong.o2: 60 days is the Sec. 9 divestment period, and April 15 is the income-tax deadline, not the SALN date.
why_wrong.o3: December 31 is the as-of date of the figures, not the filing deadline; separation filing is 30 days, not one year.
why_wrong.o4: 15 working days is the Sec. 5(a) reply period for letters; separation filing is mandatory, not on request.

items.source_quote: (a) within thirty (30) days after assumption of office; (b) on or before April 30, of every year thereafter; and (c) within thirty (30) days after separation from the service

replaces.stem: A Statement of Assets, Liabilities and Net Worth (SALN) must generally be filed:
replaces.key: Upon assumption of office, annually, and upon separation

items.micro_skill: recall and apply R.A. 6713, Sec. 3(i) and Sec. 9
items.stem: A procurement officer owns 20% of the shares of a supplier that has just bid on a contract her office will award. Under R.A. 6713, what is this situation called?

options.text: Undue favor to a relative
A conflict of interest
Divestment of a business interest
Outside employment during incumbency

reveal.terms: Conflict of interest (Sec. 3(i)): an official's private interest in a business, as a board member, officer, substantial stockholder, owner or holder of a substantial interest, may be opposed to or affected by the faithful performance of official duty.
reveal.shortcut: Own stake + your decision affects it = conflict of interest.
reveal.why_correct: Answer: A conflict of interest. Her shares give her a financial interest in a supplier whose bid her own office will decide, so her private interest can be affected by her official duty (Sec. 3(i)). The item does not depend on whether 20% makes her a "substantial stockholder" (Sec. 3(f): enough shares to elect a director). Sec. 7(a) bars any financial or material interest in a transaction requiring her office's approval, and Sec. 9 requires divestment when a conflict arises.

why_wrong.o1: Sec. 4(A)(c) concerns favors to relatives; here the interest is the officer's own.
why_wrong.o3: Divestment (Sec. 3(j)) is the cure for the conflict, not its name.
why_wrong.o4: Sec. 7(b) outside employment concerns working for a regulated firm; owning shares is not employment.

items.source_quote: "Conflict of interest" arises when a public official or employee is a member of a board, an officer, or a substantial stockholder of a private corporation or owner or has a substantial interest in a business, and the interest of such corporation or business, or his rights or duties therein, may be opposed to or affected by the faithful performance of official duty
items.shortcut: Own stake + your decision affects it = conflict of interest.

replaces.stem: Which is an example of a conflict of interest?
replaces.key: An official deciding a bid where a close relative owns a bidder

items.stem: Under R.A. 6713, a conflict of interest arises when an official is a board member, officer or substantial stockholder of a business whose interest may be what?

Owned partly by the official's relatives within the fourth degree

why_wrong.o4: The Act sets no salary-size test; the test is the effect on official duty.

items.micro_skill: recall and apply R.A. 6713, Sec. 3(j) and Sec. 9
items.stem: An official with a conflicting shareholding transfers all the shares to his wife. Under R.A. 6713, why is this NOT a valid divestment?

options.text: Divestment must be made only to the government
Shares can never be divested, only declared in the SALN
Divestment requires resigning from government first
Divestment must be in favor of someone other than the spouse and relatives

reveal.terms: Divestment (Sec. 3(j)): transfer of title by voluntarily, completely and actually giving up the right to it, to a person other than one's spouse and relatives.
reveal.shortcut: Divest = give it away outside the family.
reveal.why_correct: Answer: Divestment must be in favor of someone other than the spouse and relatives. Sec. 3(j) excludes transfers to the spouse and relatives, so moving shares to a wife leaves the conflict in the family.

why_wrong.o1: The Act does not require transfer to the government; any person other than spouse and relatives qualifies.
why_wrong.o2: Sec. 9 expressly requires divesting shareholdings within 60 days; declaring alone is not enough.
why_wrong.o3: Sec. 9 requires resigning from the private enterprise, not from government.

items.source_quote: in favor of a person or persons other than his spouse and relatives as defined in this Act
items.shortcut: Divest = give it away outside the family.

replaces.stem: Divestment under RA 6713 means:
replaces.key: Voluntarily and completely disposing of a conflicting interest

items.stem: A mayor appoints his nephew to a position. Under R.A. 6713, Sec. 4(A)(c), in which case is this NOT an undue favor to a relative?

options.text: The nephew passed the civil service examination and meets every qualification of the position
The position is strictly confidential or on the mayor's personal staff, coterminous with him
The nephew agrees to serve without any pay for the first six months of the appointment
The appointment is announced publicly on the city's website and posted at city hall

reveal.terms: Undue favor on account of office (Sec. 4(A)(c), justness and sincerity).
reveal.shortcut: Exception = confidential or coterminous personal staff.
reveal.why_correct: Answer: The position is strictly confidential or on the mayor's personal staff, coterminous with him. Sec. 4(A)(c) bars undue favors to relatives except appointments to strictly confidential positions or to personal staff whose terms are coterminous with the official.

why_wrong.o1: Eligibility is a separate requirement; it does not create the statutory exception.
why_wrong.o3: Serving without pay is not an exception in the Act.
why_wrong.o4: Publicity does not cure an undue favor.

items.source_quote: except with respect to appointments of such relatives to positions considered strictly confidential or as members of their personal staff whose terms are coterminous with theirs
items.shortcut: Exception = confidential or coterminous personal staff.

items.stem: The reviewing body finds an official's statement incomplete. Under R.A. 6713, Sec. 10(a), what must it do?

why_wrong.o2: Prosecution is not the first step for an incomplete statement under Sec. 10(a).
why_wrong.o3: Sec. 10(a) does not provide for publishing marked errors.
why_wrong.o4: The law directs correction, not treating the filing as void.

items.stem: Sustainable development is development that meets present needs without doing what?

Compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs

why_wrong.o1: Sustainable development allows resource use; it limits use that harms future generations.
why_wrong.o3: Private activity is regulated by protected-area law, not excluded by the definition.
why_wrong.o4: Population growth is not part of the definition.

Watersheds collect only rainwater that cannot be polluted

why_wrong.o2: Runoff picks up pollutants; that is why they are managed.
why_wrong.o3: Watersheds follow terrain, not political boundaries; that is why LGUs must cooperate.

items.stem: What does R.A. 9003 say about open dumps for solid waste?

They are allowed if the barangay approves them

items.stem: R.A. 9729 adopts the Precautionary Principle to guide climate risk decisions. What does that principle allow?

options.text: Taking action only after the harm is proven beyond reasonable doubt
Making the polluter pay for the cleanup after the damage has already occurred
Shifting all of the costs of climate action to developed countries alone

reveal.terms: Precautionary Principle.
reveal.shortcut: Don't wait for proof to prevent serious harm.
reveal.why_correct: Answer: Preventive action against a serious threat even without full scientific certainty. R.A. 9729 Sec. 2 names the Precautionary Principle; lack of full scientific certainty is not a reason to postpone preventive measures (see also Rule 20, A.M. No. 09-6-8-SC).

why_wrong.o3: That distorts common but differentiated responsibilities, a separate Sec. 2 principle.

Recycle materials only after they reach final disposal sites

why_wrong.o2: Recovery happens before disposal, not after.
